# Introduction

This notebook asks a single question on the finalized (res_ct = 0.2 / res_ni = 0.5)
pathology-annotated BANKSY object, restricted to the 4 pilocytic astrocytoma (PA)
samples: **does being adjacent to MAPK-high (PA-niche) glia shift a myeloid cell's
gene programs?**

For each myeloid cell we classify its local (k = 15) glial neighborhood into
{near PA-niche glia / near other glia / no glial neighbor}, compare 56 myeloid
programs across those groups, and then ask whether PA-niche proximity adds anything
beyond the neighboring glia's own MAPK dose.

**Why PA-niche glia = "MAPK-high glia".** The companion notebook `2_MAPK_adj.qmd`
(Q1) establishes that within the PA tumor lineage (astrocytes/OPCs), glia sitting in
the two PA-enriched glial niches (3 and 5) are the MAPK-high glia. So PA-niche
adjacency is the operational definition of "adjacent to MAPK-high glia" used here,
and Model 2 (below) adjusts for the glia's continuous MAPK level to test whether the
niche label is merely a MAPK proxy.

**Inference framing (important).** The models are fit *per cell*, so with thousands
of cells per group the per-cell p-values collapse and nearly every signature clears
q < 0.05 within a sample. That per-cell hit count is **not** a cohort claim -- it is
pseudoreplication. The real inferential unit here is the **sample (n = 4)**. We
therefore read this **descriptively / hypothesis-generating**: standardized effect
size + directional consistency across the 4 PA samples, not cohort-level
significance (`project_cohort_granularity`: n confounded, broad strokes only). For
calibration, a 4/4 same-direction sign test is only p = 0.125, and ~7 of 56
signatures would reach 4/4 by chance, so the all-4-consistent set is *suggestive
above chance*, not individually significant.

It is **object-free**: every cell annotation (cell type, niche, sample, histology,
alteration, x/y centroid) is read from the Phase-0 metadata TSV
(`export_new_object_cell_metadata.R`), and the imputed scores from
`MAPK_overlap_scores.csv` / `myeloid_signature_scores.csv` (Phase 1,
`1_PA_MAPK_scores.qmd`). Nothing here re-loads the 5 GB BANKSY object.

## MAPK score

```{r}
# MAPK_overlap_scores.csv: spatial (ENVI-imputed) + single-nucleus rows, each with
# cell_id, MAPK_overlap_score, cell_type (spatial = new lowercase labels; sn =
# annot_v0). Regenerated in Phase 1 against the new object's own labels.
mapk_scores = fread(paste0(out_dir, 'MAPK_overlap_scores.csv'))

# sample id + driver alteration lookup. `sample` is formatted "188570 pilocytic
# astrocytoma"; the id is always the leading digits.
mapk_scores[, sample_id := gsub('^([0-9]+).*', '\\1', sample)]
mapk_scores[, alteration := fcase(
    sample_id == '188570', 'KIAA1549::BRAF',
    sample_id == '258482', 'FGFR1 ITD',
    sample_id == '320784', 'FAM131B::BRAF',
    sample_id == '328368', 'RAF1::TOP2B'
)]
# fixed sample/alteration display order (numeric sample id order), reused by heatmaps below
alteration_levels = c('KIAA1549::BRAF', 'FGFR1 ITD', 'FAM131B::BRAF', 'RAF1::TOP2B')

# fread reads a blank CSV field as "" not NA, so normalize before is.na() filtering
mapk_scores[cell_type == '', cell_type := NA]
```

# Derive PA glial niches (programmatic, not hardcoded)

A niche qualifies as a **PA glial niche** if it is BOTH:

- **(a) PA-enriched at q < 0.05** in `niche_histology_enrichment.tsv` (glmmTMB
  log-odds vs cohort baseline). We use the odds-ratio enrichment, not raw PA
  fraction, so a niche that is glial simply because a PA sample contributes many
  of its cells does not spuriously qualify.
- **(b) glial-rich**: its PA glial fraction (astro_glial + opc + radial_glia)
  exceeds the whole-cohort glial baseline.

```{r}
cohort_glial_frac = cell_meta[, mean(cell_type %in% glial_types)]   # baseline across all 11 samples

# (b) per-niche PA glial composition
niche_comp = cell_meta_pa[, .(
    n_cells    = .N,
    glial_frac = mean(cell_type %in% glial_types),
    opc_frac   = mean(cell_type == 'opc'),
    astro_frac = mean(cell_type == 'astro_glial'),
    myeloid_frac = mean(cell_type == 'myeloid')
), niche][order(-glial_frac)]

# (a) PA enrichment from the existing niche-histology model
enr = fread(paste0(workdir, 'youyun/plgg/code/niche/proseg_output_analysis/niche_histology_enrichment.tsv'))
pa_enr = enr[histology == 'pilocytic astrocytoma',
             .(niche = as.character(niche_type), logOR = estimate_log_odds,
               q = q_value, sign_call, model_status)]

enriched_niches   = pa_enr[sign_call == 'enriched' & q < 0.05 & model_status == 'pass', niche]
glial_rich_niches = niche_comp[glial_frac > cohort_glial_frac, niche]
pa_glial_niches   = intersect(enriched_niches, glial_rich_niches)   # the derived set, used everywhere below

cat('Cohort glial baseline fraction:', round(cohort_glial_frac, 3), '\n')
cat('PA-enriched niches (q<0.05):', paste(sort(as.integer(enriched_niches)), collapse = ', '), '\n')
cat('==> PA GLIAL NICHES (enriched AND glial-rich):', paste(sort(as.integer(pa_glial_niches)), collapse = ', '), '\n')

# report the qualifying niches with their enrichment + composition
kable(
    merge(niche_comp, pa_enr, by = 'niche')[niche %in% pa_glial_niches][order(-logOR)],
    digits = 3, caption = 'Derived PA glial niches: enrichment (logOR, q) + PA composition'
)
```

# Neighborhood graph (per-sample kNN)

```{r}
k_geom = 15
# Build the kNN graph PER SAMPLE. Xenium coordinates are per-slide-local, so a
# single graph over all PA cells would create cross-sample false neighbors and
# corrupt every myeloid->glial edge. dbscan::kNN$id is n x k (column-major), so
# rep(cell_id, k) aligns row-i's k neighbors with as.vector(knn$id).
build_sample_knn = function(sdt) {
    locs = as.matrix(sdt[, .(x, y)])
    knn = dbscan::kNN(x = locs, k = k_geom)
    data.table(
        from_id   = rep(sdt$cell_id, k_geom),
        to_id     = sdt$cell_id[as.vector(knn$id)],
        distance  = as.vector(knn$dist),
        sample_id = sdt$sample_id[1]
    )
}
knnDT = rbindlist(lapply(split(cell_meta_pa, by = 'sample_id'), build_sample_knn))

# annotate each edge with from/to cell type, straight from the TSV (no cluster->label map)
adjacencies = merge(knnDT, cell_meta_pa[, .(to_id = cell_id, cell_type_to = cell_type)], by = 'to_id')
adjacencies = merge(adjacencies, cell_meta_pa[, .(from_id = cell_id, cell_type_from = cell_type)], by = 'from_id')
# sanity: per-sample construction must produce zero cross-sample edges
stopifnot(adjacencies[gsub('.*__', '', from_id) != gsub('.*__', '', to_id), .N] == 0)
cat('kNN edges:', nrow(adjacencies), '| myeloid source cells:',
    adjacencies[cell_type_from == 'myeloid', uniqueN(from_id)], '\n')
```

# Myeloid programs by glial neighborhood

For each myeloid cell we classify its glial neighborhood:

- **pa_niche_glia** -- >=1 glial neighbor whose niche is a PA glial niche
- **other_glia** -- has glial neighbor(s), but none in a PA niche
- **no_glial** -- no glial neighbor at all

We fit two models per sample x signature:

- **Model 1 (primary, all myeloid cells):** `signature ~ exposure_group`,
  reference = `other_glia`, so the `pa_niche_glia` coefficient is the direct
  PA-specific effect (does PA-tumor-niche glial exposure shift the program beyond
  generic glial exposure?).
- **Model 2 (refinement, glia-adjacent cells only):**
  `signature ~ (pa_niche_glia vs other_glia) + mean_glial_mapk`. The MAPK dose is
  undefined for no-glial cells, so they are dropped here. This asks whether
  PA-niche proximity adds anything *beyond* the glial cells' own MAPK level.

Signatures (56: 50 MSigDB Hallmark + 6 myeloid/immune literature sets) are
z-scored within each patient before fitting.

**Contrast structure.** Because the PA glial niches (3/5) hold most glial cells in
PA, most glia-adjacent myeloid cells land in `pa_niche_glia` (a broad tumor-core
tent) while `other_glia` is a smaller tumor-periphery group. This imbalance is the
intended tumor-core-vs-periphery contrast, by design, not a defect.

## Build myeloid glial-exposure table

```{r}
glial_mapk_lookup  = mapk_scores[type == 'spatial', .(cell_id, glial_mapk = MAPK_overlap_score)]
glial_niche_lookup = cell_meta_pa[cell_type %in% glial_types, .(to_id = cell_id, to_niche = niche)]

# myeloid -> glial directed edges, tagged with each glial neighbor's niche + MAPK
myeloid_glial_edges = adjacencies[cell_type_from == 'myeloid' & cell_type_to %in% glial_types]
myeloid_glial_edges = merge(myeloid_glial_edges, glial_niche_lookup, by = 'to_id')
myeloid_glial_edges = merge(myeloid_glial_edges, glial_mapk_lookup, by.x = 'to_id', by.y = 'cell_id')
myeloid_glial_edges[, to_in_pa_niche := to_niche %in% pa_glial_niches]

# aggregate per myeloid cell: glial-neighbor count, PA-niche-glial count, mean glial MAPK
glial_agg = myeloid_glial_edges[, .(
    n_glial         = .N,
    n_pa_glial      = sum(to_in_pa_niche),
    mean_glial_mapk = mean(glial_mapk)      # over ALL glial neighbors -> Model 2 dose covariate
), .(cell_id = from_id, sample_id)]

# keep every myeloid cell, including those with zero glial neighbors
all_myeloid = unique(adjacencies[cell_type_from == 'myeloid', .(cell_id = from_id, sample_id)])
myeloid_exposure = merge(all_myeloid, glial_agg, by = c('cell_id', 'sample_id'), all.x = TRUE)
myeloid_exposure[is.na(n_glial), `:=`(n_glial = 0L, n_pa_glial = 0L, mean_glial_mapk = NA_real_)]
myeloid_exposure[, exposure_group := fcase(
    n_pa_glial >= 1, 'pa_niche_glia',
    n_glial   >= 1,  'other_glia',
    default = 'no_glial'
)]
# reference = other_glia so the pa_niche_glia coefficient is the PA-specific effect
myeloid_exposure[, exposure_group := factor(exposure_group, levels = c('other_glia', 'pa_niche_glia', 'no_glial'))]
myeloid_exposure[, sample_id := as.character(sample_id)]

# per-sample group counts (feasibility of Model 1 / Model 2 per sample)
group_counts = dcast(myeloid_exposure[, .N, .(sample_id, exposure_group)],
                     sample_id ~ exposure_group, value.var = 'N', fill = 0)
cat('Myeloid exposure-group counts per sample:\n'); print(group_counts)
fwrite(myeloid_exposure, paste0(out_dir, 'myeloid_glial_exposure.tsv'), sep = '\t')
```

## Load myeloid signature scores and z-score per patient

```{r}
# myeloid_signature_scores.csv: myeloid cells x 56 score columns + cell_id + sample_id
# (Phase 1: sc.tl.score_genes on the spatial ENVI imputation, subset to new myeloid label).
sig_scores = fread(paste0(out_dir, 'myeloid_signature_scores.csv'))
score_cols = grep('_score$', names(sig_scores), value = TRUE)
sig_scores[, sample_id := as.character(sample_id)]

myeloid_data = merge(
    myeloid_exposure,
    sig_scores[, c('cell_id', 'sample_id', score_cols), with = FALSE],
    by = c('cell_id', 'sample_id')
)
cat(sprintf('Joined %d / %d myeloid cells to signature scores (%.1f%% match); %d signatures.\n',
            nrow(myeloid_data), nrow(myeloid_exposure),
            100 * nrow(myeloid_data) / nrow(myeloid_exposure), length(score_cols)))

# z-score each signature within each patient (per-sample score_genes baselines)
myeloid_data[
    , (score_cols) := lapply(.SD, function(x) (x - mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(x, na.rm = TRUE))
    , .SDcols = score_cols, by = sample_id
]
```

## Fit both models

```{r}
#| results: hold
MIN_N_GRP = 30   # min cells per contrasted group

# Fit lm(sig ~ rhs) and return the single coefficient whose term == term_keep.
# Name-based selection (unlike a single-predictor helper) so it works with the
# 3-level factor and the covariate-adjusted model.
fit_term_row = function(dt, sig_col, rhs, term_keep, weight_col = NULL) {
    fml = as.formula(paste0('`', sig_col, '` ~ ', rhs))
    wts = if (!is.null(weight_col)) dt[[weight_col]] else NULL
    m = tryCatch(lm(fml, data = dt, weights = wts), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(m)) return(NULL)
    co = as.data.table(summary(m)$coefficients, keep.rownames = 'term')
    row = co[term == term_keep]
    if (nrow(row) != 1) return(NULL)
    data.table(signature = sig_col, Estimate = row$Estimate, SE = row[['Std. Error']],
               t_value = row[['t value']], p_value = row[['Pr(>|t|)']], n_cells = nrow(dt))
}

# empty, correctly-typed results table (so BH/merge don't error if nothing fits)
empty_results = function() data.table(
    signature = character(0), Estimate = numeric(0), SE = numeric(0), t_value = numeric(0),
    p_value = numeric(0), n_cells = integer(0), sample_id = character(0),
    q_value = numeric(0), alteration = factor(character(0), levels = alteration_levels)
)

finalize = function(res, path) {
    if (nrow(res) == 0 || !'sample_id' %in% names(res)) {
        res = empty_results()
    } else {
        res[, q_value := p.adjust(p_value, method = 'BH'), by = sample_id]
        res = merge(res, unique(mapk_scores[, .(sample_id, alteration)]), by = 'sample_id')
        res[, alteration := factor(alteration, levels = alteration_levels)]
    }
    fwrite(res, path, sep = '\t')
    res
}

samples = unique(myeloid_data$sample_id)

# --- Model 1: 3-group, all myeloid cells, PA-niche-glia vs other-glia ---------
combos = CJ(sample_id = samples, signature = score_cols)
nested_results = rbindlist(mapply(function(sid, sig) {
    dt = myeloid_data[sample_id == sid, .SD, .SDcols = c(sig, 'exposure_group')]
    dt = dt[complete.cases(dt)]
    dt[, exposure_group := droplevels(exposure_group)]
    # need both the reference (other_glia) and pa_niche_glia populated
    if (dt[exposure_group == 'pa_niche_glia', .N] < MIN_N_GRP ||
        dt[exposure_group == 'other_glia',   .N] < MIN_N_GRP) return(NULL)
    res = fit_term_row(dt, sig, 'exposure_group', 'exposure_grouppa_niche_glia')
    if (!is.null(res)) res[, sample_id := sid]
    res
}, combos$sample_id, combos$signature, SIMPLIFY = FALSE))
nested_results = finalize(nested_results, paste0(out_dir, 'myeloid_glial_exposure_nested_results.tsv'))
cat('Model 1 (3-group): significant (q<0.05) signature-patient hits:',
    sum(nested_results$q_value < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), '\n')

# --- Model 2: covariate-adjusted, glia-adjacent cells only --------------------
# drop no_glial (mean_glial_mapk undefined); binary pa vs other + MAPK dose
adj_base = myeloid_data[exposure_group %in% c('pa_niche_glia', 'other_glia')]
adj_base[, exposure_group := droplevels(exposure_group)]   # reference = other_glia
covar_results = rbindlist(mapply(function(sid, sig) {
    dt = adj_base[sample_id == sid, .SD, .SDcols = c(sig, 'exposure_group', 'mean_glial_mapk')]
    dt = dt[complete.cases(dt)]
    if (dt[exposure_group == 'pa_niche_glia', .N] < MIN_N_GRP ||
        dt[exposure_group == 'other_glia',   .N] < MIN_N_GRP) return(NULL)
    res = fit_term_row(dt, sig, 'exposure_group + mean_glial_mapk', 'exposure_grouppa_niche_glia')
    if (!is.null(res)) res[, sample_id := sid]
    res
}, combos$sample_id, combos$signature, SIMPLIFY = FALSE))
covar_results = finalize(covar_results, paste0(out_dir, 'myeloid_glial_exposure_covariate_results.tsv'))
cat('Model 2 (MAPK-adjusted): significant (q<0.05) signature-patient hits:',
    sum(covar_results$q_value < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), '\n')
```

## Cohort readout: effect size + cross-sample consistency (the headline answer)

The per-cell q<0.05 hit counts above are **within-sample descriptive only** and are
dominated by pseudoreplication (thousands of cells per group ⇒ SEs collapse). The
cohort-level answer is read off the **per-sample standardized effect sizes** and
their **directional consistency across the 4 PA samples**. A signature is
"all-4-consistent" if it was fittable in all 4 samples and every per-sample beta
shares the same sign. Calibration: ~7 of 56 signatures would reach 4/4 by chance,
so this set is *suggestive above chance*, not individually significant at n=4.

```{r}
# Collapse per-sample betas to one row per signature: directional consistency +
# mean standardized effect. Uses ALL fitted per-sample betas (not the per-cell
# q-value), because the sample is the inferential unit here.
q2_consistency = function(res, label) {
    if (nrow(res) == 0) return(data.table(signature = character(0)))
    s = res[!is.na(Estimate), .(
        n_samples = .N,                       # samples where the contrast was fittable (N>=MIN_N_GRP)
        n_pos     = sum(Estimate > 0),
        n_neg     = sum(Estimate < 0),
        mean_beta = mean(Estimate)            # mean standardized effect across samples
    ), by = signature]
    s[, consistent_4 := n_samples == 4L & (n_pos == 4L | n_neg == 4L)]
    s[, model := label]
    s[order(-consistent_4, -abs(mean_beta))]
}
nested_consistency = q2_consistency(nested_results, 'Model1_3group')
covar_consistency  = q2_consistency(covar_results,  'Model2_MAPKadj')

# Headline table: the all-4-consistent signatures under Model 1, most-affected first.
headline = nested_consistency[consistent_4 == TRUE][order(-abs(mean_beta))]
cat('All-4-sample-consistent signatures (Model 1):', nrow(headline),
    '(vs ~7 expected by chance across 56)\n')
kable(headline[, .(signature = sub('_score$', '', signature),
                   direction = ifelse(mean_beta > 0, 'up', 'down'),
                   mean_beta = round(mean_beta, 3))],
      caption = 'Headline: myeloid programs consistently shifted near PA-niche glia across all 4 PA samples')

# Model 2 attenuation: how much does adjusting for neighbor-glial MAPK dose shrink
# the PA-niche effect on this consistent set? Persistence (small attenuation) is the
# evidence that PA-niche proximity is not merely a proxy for the glia's MAPK level.
atten = merge(
    headline[, .(signature, beta_m1 = mean_beta)],
    covar_consistency[, .(signature, beta_m2 = mean_beta)],
    by = 'signature')
atten[, atten_pct := round(100 * (1 - beta_m2 / beta_m1), 1)]   # % shrink of |effect| under MAPK adjustment
cat(sprintf('Model 2 attenuation over the consistent set: median %.0f%% (IQR %.0f-%.0f%%); %d/%d retain sign.\n',
            median(atten$atten_pct, na.rm = TRUE),
            quantile(atten$atten_pct, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
            quantile(atten$atten_pct, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
            atten[sign(beta_m2) == sign(beta_m1), .N], nrow(atten)))
kable(atten[order(-abs(beta_m1)), .(signature = sub('_score$', '', signature),
            beta_model1 = round(beta_m1, 3), beta_model2 = round(beta_m2, 3),
            attenuation_pct = atten_pct)],
      caption = 'PA-niche effect attenuates modestly but persists after adjusting for glial MAPK dose')
```

**Reading this.** The PA-niche myeloid shift is carried by the all-4-consistent set,
not by the raw per-cell hit count. Under MAPK adjustment (Model 2) those effects
attenuate only modestly and keep their sign — so neighbor-glial MAPK dose explains
part but not most of the signal, and PA-niche proximity is not simply a MAPK proxy.

### Interpretation

The **20 of 56** signatures that move the same direction in all 4 PA samples (~7 expected
by chance ⇒ ~3× enrichment; per-cell q is pseudoreplicated and not the claim) split into
two coherent, biologically consistent themes — myeloid cells near PA-niche glia (the tumor
core), relative to myeloid near other glia (periphery):

- **Immunosuppressive / alternatively-activated TAM shift** — ↓ inflammatory response,
  ↓ IFN-γ response, ↓ allograft rejection, ↓ homeostatic (TIM3-neg) microglia, ↓ FOSL2
  regulon; ↑ complement, ↑ activated-microglia (MG_Act). A pull away from pro-inflammatory/
  antigen-presenting microglia toward a complement-high, immunosuppressive-leaning TAM state.
- **Metabolic reprogramming** — ↓ glycolysis, ↓ hypoxia, ↓ PI3K–AKT–mTOR, ↓ apoptosis;
  ↑ heme metabolism, ↑ adipogenesis (lipid), ↑ xenobiotic metabolism, ↑ coagulation. A switch
  from glycolytic/hypoxic signaling toward lipid/heme scavenging — the metabolic signature of
  scavenger/anti-inflammatory macrophages.

Because these persist under MAPK adjustment (Model 2: ~9% median attenuation, 20/20 keep
sign), the phenotype tracks **PA-niche proximity itself, not the neighboring glia's MAPK
dose**. Caveat: n = 4 (suggestive/hypothesis-generating, not cohort-significant), ENVI-imputed
on a 266-gene panel.

## Heatmaps

Signatures sorted by mean |beta| across patients (most-affected at top). Bold
rows = myeloid/immune-specific signatures; plain = generic Hallmark controls.
Fill = standardized beta where the **within-sample** per-cell q < 0.05 (BH per
patient); grey = n.s. The per-cell q here is descriptive within each sample (it is
inflated by pseudoreplication) — the cohort-level answer is the all-4-consistent
set in the table above, and these heatmaps show the per-sample effect **sizes** and
their sign agreement across the 4 columns.

```{r}
immune_sigs = c(

plot_exposure_heatmap = function(results_dt, title, subtitle) {
    if (nrow(results_dt) == 0) {
        return(ggplot() +
            annotate('text', x = 0.5, y = 0.5, size = 4.5, color = 'grey30',
                     label = paste0(title, '\n\n(no fitted rows: contrasted groups under-populated in this cohort)')) +
            theme_void())
    }
    dt = copy(results_dt)
    dt[, sig_label := sub('_score$', '', signature)]
    row_order = dt[, .(mean_abs = mean(abs(Estimate), na.rm = TRUE)), sig_label][order(-mean_abs)]$sig_label
    dt[, sig_label := factor(sig_label, levels = row_order)]
    dt[, fill_val := ifelse(q_value < 0.05, Estimate, NA_real_)]
    is_immune = sub('_score$', '', immune_sigs)
    face_vec = ifelse(levels(dt$sig_label) %in% is_immune, 'bold', 'plain')

    ggplot(dt, aes(x = alteration, y = sig_label, fill = fill_val)) +
        geom_tile(color = 'white', linewidth = 0.6) +
        scale_fill_gradient2(low = '#2166ac', mid = '#f7f7f7', high = '#b2182b', midpoint = 0,
                             na.value = 'grey92', limits = c(-1, 1), name = 'Standardized\nbeta (q<0.05)') +
        scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(add = 0.6)) +
        scale_y_discrete(expand = expansion(add = 0.6)) +
        labs(title = title, subtitle = subtitle) +
        theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
        theme(axis.title = element_blank(),
              axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 11),
              axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8, face = face_vec),
              panel.grid = element_blank(),
              plot.title = element_text(face = 'bold', size = 14, margin = margin(b = 4)),
              plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, color = 'grey40', margin = margin(b = 8)),
              legend.title = element_text(size = 9), legend.key.height = unit(1.4, 'lines'))
}

plot_exposure_heatmap(
    nested_results,
    'Model 1: PA-niche-glial vs other-glial exposure on myeloid programs',
    'Fill: beta for pa_niche_glia vs other_glia (reference), z-scored signature, all myeloid cells.\nBold = myeloid/immune-specific; plain = generic Hallmark controls.'
)
```

## Focused figure: the immunosuppressive-TAM axis

A compact, publication-ready view of the four programs that best summarize the shift
in myeloid state near MAPK-high (PA-niche) glia: **Complement** and **activated
microglia (MG_Act)** up, **inflammatory response** and **IFN-γ response** down. Each
row is marked with its **sample-level** significance — a one-sample t-test on the four
per-sample betas, BH-corrected across all 56 signatures (`* q<0.05`, `** q<0.01`). This
is the honest inferential unit (sample, n=4); the per-cell q is deliberately not used
because it is pseudoreplicated. Only Complement and MG_Act survive that correction, so
they carry the `**`/`*` marks; inflammatory/IFN-γ are directionally consistent (4/4) but
not significant at the sample level. Saved as vector PDF + 300 dpi PNG.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8.4
#| fig-height: 4.0
# Four programs summarizing the immunosuppressive/activated-TAM <-> pro-inflammatory
# axis near MAPK-high (PA-niche) glia. Uses the in-memory Model-1 results
# (nested_results); saves vector PDF + 300 dpi PNG for figure use.
focus_map = c(
    'HALLMARK_COMPLEMENT_score'                = 'Complement',
    'MG_Act_Tripathi_score'                    = 'Activated microglia (MG_Act)',
    'HALLMARK_INFLAMMATORY_RESPONSE_score'     = 'Inflammatory response',
    'HALLMARK_INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE_score' = 'IFN-γ response'
)
# top-to-bottom row order: the two up-regulated programs above the two down-regulated
order_sig = c('HALLMARK_COMPLEMENT_score', 'MG_Act_Tripathi_score',
              'HALLMARK_INFLAMMATORY_RESPONSE_score', 'HALLMARK_INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE_score')

# Sample-level significance (honest unit = sample, n=4): one-sample t-test on each
# signature's per-sample betas, BH across all 56. Per-cell q is NOT used (pseudoreplicated).
sig_sample = nested_results[!is.na(Estimate), .(t_p = if (.N >= 2) t.test(Estimate)$p.value else NA_real_), signature]
sig_sample[, t_q := p.adjust(t_p, 'BH')]
star_of = function(q) fifelse(is.na(q), '',
                       fifelse(q < 0.001, '***', fifelse(q < 0.01, '**', fifelse(q < 0.05, '*', ''))))
star_map = setNames(star_of(sig_sample$t_q), sig_sample$signature)

# display label = program name + its sample-level star (y labels are right-aligned, so
# the trailing stars line up flush against the tiles)
lab_of = function(s) { st = star_map[[s]]; if (nzchar(st)) paste0(focus_map[[s]], '  ', st) else focus_map[[s]] }
lab_top_to_bottom = vapply(order_sig, lab_of, character(1))

fdt = nested_results[signature %in% names(focus_map)]
fdt[, sig_disp := vapply(signature, lab_of, character(1))]

# per-sample betas + a Mean(n=4) summary column; a blank spacer level gives a visual gap
per = fdt[, .(sig_disp, col = as.character(alteration), beta = Estimate)]
mn  = fdt[, .(col = 'Mean (n=4)', beta = mean(Estimate)), sig_disp]
pd  = rbind(per, mn)
pd[, col := factor(col, levels = c(alteration_levels, ' ', 'Mean (n=4)'))]  # ' ' = empty gap col
pd[, sig_disp := factor(sig_disp, levels = rev(lab_top_to_bottom))]         # rev: first level plots at bottom

lim = 0.55   # symmetric diverging limit; the one RAF1 inflammatory cell (~ -1.05) is squished
p_focus = ggplot(pd, aes(col, sig_disp, fill = beta)) +
    geom_tile(color = 'white', linewidth = 1.4) +
    # beta printed in each cell; white text on saturated tiles, dark on pale ones
    geom_text(aes(label = sprintf('%+.2f', beta), color = abs(beta) > 0.28),
              fontface = 'bold', size = 3.6, show.legend = FALSE, na.rm = TRUE) +
    # oob = squish: clamp the out-of-range RAF1 inflammatory cell to the end color instead
    # of censoring it to grey; its numeric value is still printed
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = '#2166ac', mid = '#f7f7f7', high = '#b2182b', midpoint = 0,
                         limits = c(-lim, lim), breaks = c(-0.5, 0, 0.5),
                         oob = scales::squish, name = 'Standardized β') +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 'white', `FALSE` = 'grey20')) +
    scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE, expand = expansion(add = 0)) +
    scale_y_discrete(expand = expansion(add = 0)) +
    labs(title = 'Myeloid programs shift near MAPK-high (PA-niche) glia',
         subtitle = 'Standardized β: near PA-niche vs other glia (Model 1) · same direction in all 4 PA samples',
         caption = 'Row marks = sample-level significance: one-sample t-test on per-sample β, BH across 56 signatures (* q<0.05, ** q<0.01).\nPer-cell q omitted (pseudoreplicated). n = 4 PA samples, ENVI-imputed.',
         x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1, size = 10, color = 'grey20'),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 11, color = 'grey15'),
        panel.grid = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(face = 'bold', size = 13, margin = margin(b = 3)),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, color = 'grey40', margin = margin(b = 10)),
        plot.caption = element_text(size = 7.5, color = 'grey45', hjust = 0, margin = margin(t = 8)),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 10),
        legend.key.height = unit(1.1, 'lines'),
        plot.margin = margin(10, 14, 8, 10)
    )

ggsave(paste0(out_dir, 'fig_myeloid_glial_exposure_focus4.png'), p_focus,
       width = 8.4, height = 4.0, dpi = 300, device = ragg::agg_png)
ggsave(paste0(out_dir, 'fig_myeloid_glial_exposure_focus4.pdf'), p_focus,
       width = 8.4, height = 4.0, device = cairo_pdf)
p_focus
```
